ashley: Heads up — quickstart http handler pattern with generator.Stream sometimes keeps the process alive in CI. Minimal pattern we ship:
```go
func Handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  gen := client.Generator("redwood/small")
  s, _ := gen.Stream(r.Context(), "hi")
  defer s.Close()
  go func(){
    for b := range s.Chunks() { w.Write(b) }
  }()
  return
}
```
ashley: Locally ok; CI shows lambda/runtime waits 1-2s after return. Stack shows goroutines stuck in generator.handshake and auth.refresh.
mike: Likely two issues: handshake doesn't select on ctx.Done(), auth refresh holds dedupe mutex across network. Both stop early cancellation.
zara: Proposal: make handshake accept ctx and select on ctx.Done() when waiting for HTTP resp. Change token refresh to not hold mutex while doing network I/O (double-check lock).
mike: Could add StreamWithContext(ctx) helper so handlers can pass r.Context() explicitly and users don't need to manage extra cancel funcs. Also document the pattern that handlers should wait for stream completion unless they intentionally detach.
ashley: I'll open a tiny repro and tests: spawn Stream in goroutine, cancel ctx, assert goroutines exit within 100ms. If folks agree, I'll PR small changes and docs.
devx-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-1812 and attached the trace.
